CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. James is a 42-year-old female who presents with right index finger pain sustained approximately 5 days ago while skiing double black diamond slopes. She lost control while skiing and flipped down the slope, jamming her right index finger on an unknown object. Pain is rated 7/10. She has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. She has not applied ice or splint to the finger. She denies other injuries from the fall.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation. Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation. Ibuprofen taken for finger pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger: Tender to palpation. Pain with traction. Pain with squeezing over joints.

RESULTS
Right hand X-ray: Normal. No fractures. All bones and joints in appropriate alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Patient will be placed in a splint on the right index finger. Mobic 15 mg once daily prescribed for 14 tablets. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed.
